name: Concatenating Strings and Numbers (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that uses variables x, y, and z to print "10 + 20 = 30".
code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables x, y, and z
x = 10
y = 20
z = x + y
#Step 2: Print the text using the variables initialized above 
print(str(x) + " + " + str(y) + " = " + str(z))

comments.content: This statement sets variable x to the integer 10.
This statement sets variable y to the integer 20.
This statement sets variable z to the integer value that is the result of the addition operation.

The expression on the right-hand side of the assignment operator adds the values stored in variable x and y. The result of the addition is an integer value because both operands of the addition operator are integers. Note that variables x and y have an integer value.

This statement concatenates the content of variables x, y, and z to print the requested output. We concatenate the content of these variables using the + operator. All three variables have integer values and their values could be concatenated with strings only when they are explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't necessarily have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
